question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=\frac{5}{\sqrt{2x+1}}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=\frac{5}{\sqrt{2y+1}}.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{5}{\sqrt{2y+1}} \\ \sqrt{2y+1} & =\frac{5}{x} \\ (\sqrt{2y+1})^{2} & ={(\frac{5}{x})}^{2} \\ 2y+1 & =\frac{25}{{x}^{2}} \\ 2y & =\frac{25}{{x}^{2}}-1 \\ y & =\frac{25}{2{x}^{2}}-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{25}{2{x}^{2}}-\frac{1}{2}.
$$

**Note**: The domain and range of $f(x)$ are

$$
x>-\frac{1}{2},\,f(x)>0.
$$

Therefore, the domain and range of ${f}^{-1}(x)$ are

$$
x>0,\,{f}^{-1}(x)>-\frac{1}{2}.
$$
